Seasonal Wildlife · the full-pool design · desk simulation · 9 Oct 2026

Cast Pipeline Trace

Your design of 9 Oct (evening), simulated on DF's own raws for six embarks. The pool is no longer the short list DF stocked on the region: every creature in the raws is a candidate, filtered first by wild and natural, then BIOME, SAVAGE, GOOD/EVIL and the world's real-world-extinct rule, then split into seven layers (land-ground, land-flying, ocean, freshwater, cavern 1, 2, 3) and four seasons. Each of those lists feeds one season cast with the slot table you set for its layer. Nothing here ran DF and the engine is unchanged; this is the design, ahead of building it. Every table sorts by a click on its header; categorical columns filter.

What changes, in numbers

Land-ground pools grow several-fold

6 → 19 species on the lake fort, 3 → 24 on the ocean fort: what DF stocked against everything the biome allows.

Every species DF stocked is still in

On all three real forts the new pool contains every species in DF's population list, except the locked unliving cave species, the lava-only magma crab, demons, and one damselfly. The biome reading matches DF's own stocking.

Variety across the year

19 different species cast on the lake fort's land-ground over four seasons, 27 in the ocean fort's sea. The x0.01-per-earlier-cast weight spreads the picks.

Caverns get stranger with depth

Mean weirdness of the casts: cavern 1 0.23, cavern 2 0.51, cavern 3 0.74 (0 = a real animal's cave form, 1 = wholly alien).

Six embarks

Three real forts on region19: their land biomes are the 3×3 world tiles around the fort (from the world survey), their water bodies come from the tool's own map scan, and the temperature zone of their rivers and pools is read from the water species DF stocked there. Three synthetic embarks cover the other cases: an arctic coast with a river and extinct creatures in any wild region; a savage lake; an evil savanna with murky pools only.

The top-level filters

All 967 creatures in the raws (vanilla and extinct files, giants and animal people included) through the gates. "Wild" is DF's own test for region populations: a BIOME, and LARGE_ROAMING or a vermin tag (colony insects included). It drops 29 creatures: domestic animals and civilised races (no BIOME), the three DOES_NOT_EXIST entries and the wagon, and the megabeasts and titans (dragon, hydra, roc, colossus, cyclops, ettin, giant, minotaur). The sponge passes as a placed plant. "Natural" drops 12 unliving: the elemental men and blood man, fire imp and fire snake, grimeling, nightwing and purring maggot. Kept (12 Oct): the sponge and giant sponge as plants placed on the bed (no cast slot), the sponge man as a filter-feeding creature. The 28 GOOD and EVIL species stay in until the alignment gate, which checks each biome.

What the six embarks show

  • The diversity is there. The lake fort's land-ground pool is 19 species where DF stocked 6; the savage forest's is 226 (its extinct species, giants and animal people all qualify). The casts stay the size you set; the variety shows across the year.
  • A marsh has few walkers. The brook fort's land-ground pool is 6 species: most marsh animals are amphibious and now belong to the water layer, as you ruled. Its freshwater pool is 20.
  • The apex rotates. Under the rebuilt rule the apex differs between seasons on 32 of the 34 layers with an apex slot. The ocean fort's sea goes orca → sperm whale → shark mako longfin → shark blue; the arctic coast's land bear polar → bear grizzly → bear polar → wolf. Where it stays put, only one predator is eligible: the dingo is the only flagged hunter of a temperate savanna or marsh in DF's raws (lake and brook forts).
  • Murky pools work as a mini roster once the pool's fish slot can draw DF's pool fish and amphibians, which are all vermin: on the evil savanna the year casts FISH_LUNGFISH, LEECH, POND_TURTLE, RIVER OTTER, TOAD.
  • River-only freshwater has no apex, as you listed; the alligator and similar predators take its one meso slot.
  • Extinct species follow the world setting. With "any wild region" the arctic coast gains 14 extinct species (woolly mammoth and woolly rhinoceros among them); with "savage regions only" the calm real forts get none and the savage forest gets all that fit.
  • Odd fits come from DF's own raws, not the filter: an alligator on a cold river (its raws allow any temperate river), a capybara on a temperate saltwater marsh, penguins on an arctic coast.
  • Caverns are the same three pools on every fort (DF's cave species are not biome-bound), so only the draw differs between forts.

Who can hold the apex

Rebuilt 10 Oct. A species can be drawn for the apex slot of a layer when it is:

  • a LARGE_PREDATOR species (land, flying and caverns; caverns keep their sentients in the sentient slot);
  • a giant of any predator, mesopredators included (giant fox, giant badger, giant kestrel);
  • an animal person whose root animal is eligible (bear man, cougar man, quetzalcoatlus man), drawn at x0.1 as all animal people;
  • on water layers, one of the engine's curated water apexes (orca, sperm whale, great white, crocodiles, the large sharks) or a giant or animal person of one; DF's other LARGE_PREDATOR water species (sea lamprey, frill shark, blacktip) take meso, as before;
  • a raptor of 2,000 cm³ or more on land-flying (eagle, the large owls, osprey; never a scavenger);
  • a real-life apex that DF does not tag, below.

The draw then weights each by the square root of its group size against the largest (a pack's mean size times the adult size), x3 for pack hunters, x0.01 for each cast it is already on this year (counted only once drawn: the year's 28 casts are built together at its start), x0.2 giants and x0.1 animal people. That is what puts the orca beside the sperm whale: a pod of six orcas outweighs one whale.

Real-life apexes DF does not tag LARGE_PREDATOR

Every carnivore in the raws without the flag (56) and the large predators DF does not even mark CARNIVORE were checked against their real ecology. "Apex" joins the draw; "local" holds the apex only where no true apex is in season (the top of a small or depleted community). Several are not CARNIVORE in DF's raws; the CARNIVORE fix below now reads them as predators.

The CARNIVORE fix

Real-life hunters DF does not tag CARNIVORE (or BONECARN), which the tool used to read as prey (12 Oct: applied). Upper-level predators only: mid-level fish (cod, carp, bluefish, skate) stay in the fish slot and penguins stay shore birds. A fish-eating bird gains the predator role but is not a raptor, so it never holds the flying apex. In the engine this is a set of 'predator' entries in MODEL.ROLE.

Biomes × region × apex audit

Built programmatically over the whole creature list (scripts/castsim/apex_audit.py): every surface biome (27 land, 3 oceans, temperate and tropical lakes) under six region types (not savage or savage, × good, neutral or evil; extinct species under UNTAMED_WILDS, so only on savage regions), through the same filters and layer split as the casts. For each it counts the layer's potential cast members and, per season, the species that can hold the apex. A row is short when some season has fewer than two true apexes. Rivers and murky pools have no apex slot; caverns do not depend on the region.

Candidates for the short rows

Generated, not hand-picked. Promote: every resident predator that cannot hold the apex today, the resident local apexes (lynx, coyote, wolverine) first, then by group size against the largest resident. Wire: every species that is a true apex of the same layer in another biome of the same region type and climate band, scored by fauna overlap (the share of this biome's residents that also live in the candidate's biomes). The automatic proposal takes local promotions, then wires with overlap 0.5 or more, then other promotions, then other wires, until every season has two true apexes. The scores say how well a candidate fits DF's own fauna, not real-life range: a wired dingo in the taiga scores well because DF's dingo shares most of the taiga's animals. Not applied to the casts on this page.

Judgement calls in this simulation

Everything the design left open and the simulation had to decide. Each is a single rule you can change.

decisionwhat the simulation does
land-ground slotsnot specified: kept the v7.4 land cast without its raptor, bird and sentient slots (apex 1, meso 2, grazer 2, ground prey 2, vermin 3).
ranges"1-2" and "2-3": each cast draws its count inside the range, so cast sizes vary from season to season.
apex rulerebuilt 10 Oct: the apex is a weighted draw among the eligible predators in season, not the largest. Eligible: LARGE_PREDATOR species, giants of any predator, animal people whose root is eligible, the curated water apexes, raptors of 2,000 cm3 and up, and the real-life apexes DF does not flag (table on the page). Weight: the square root of group size (adult size x the pack's mean size) against the largest, x3 for pack hunters, x0.01 per cast the species is already on this year, x0.2 giants, x0.1 animal people. No size floor (a 10% floor cut lions and hyenas beside a pair of ogres, and the great white beside an orca pod). The rest can still take meso. Water layers: only the curated water apexes (and their giants and animal people) are eligible, as in the engine; DF's other LARGE_PREDATOR water species (sea lamprey, frill shark, blacktip) take meso.
local apexesa "local" real-life apex (lynx, coyote, wolverine, gar, grouper...) holds the apex only when no true apex is in season; with none of either, the largest non-sentient predator is promoted (the old fallback, still your open question).
spongesthe sponge and the giant sponge are placed like plants on the bed (30 Sep, 12 Oct): they pass the filters, enter the water layers they live in, and take no cast slot; the sponge man passes as a natural filter-feeder creature and can be cast.
CARNIVORE fixreal-life hunters DF does not tag CARNIVORE are read as predators (table on the page): upper-level fish and small sharks, seals, walrus, mink, weasel, fish-eating seabirds and the white stork. Mid-level fish (cod, carp, bluefish, skate) and penguins are left as they were.
reusex0.01 per cast the species is already on this year (12 Oct; was x0.1). It counts only casts already drawn: all 28 casts of a year are built at once at the start of the year, layer by layer, season by season, so a species is penalised only after it has been drawn.
river-only apexno apex slot (your list has none); flagged predators there can take the meso slot.
fill fallbacka slot with room and no candidate linked to the cast is filled anyway from its eligible species ("no link"), so no slot stays empty while candidates exist; the food web is computed after the draw on every layer, as you asked for land-flying.
amphibiansan amphibious (water-breathing, not aquatic) creature never enters land-ground; if its BIOME names a fort land biome it can enter the freshwater layer (its shore slot), and on a saltwater marsh, swamp or mangrove the ocean layer.
shore and fliersa shore creature or a waterbird eats an aquatic creature no larger than itself (or 20,000 cm3), and aquatic vermin.
murky pools"small" = adult size up to 20,000 cm3 for the pool mini roster; DF's pool fish and amphibians are vermin (lungfish, pond turtle, toad), so the pool's fish slot draws fish-class and amphibious vermin too (a species drawn as fish is not also drawn as vermin).
cavern sentientsa sentient cavern species (troll, blind cave ogre, gorlak, animal people, troglodyte) fills only the sentient slot.
weirdnessa first-cut 0-1 score per cavern species (table in the step-through); cavern 1 picks weight (1-w)^2, cavern 2 the middle, cavern 3 w^2. DF's own raw depth range still decides which caverns a species can live in.
region biomesa real fort's biomes are the 3x3 world tiles around it (DF draws a block's wildlife from all nine region neighbours); each biome takes the savagery and evil of the nearest tile that has it.
alignmentGOOD species only where the biome is good (evil 0-32), EVIL only where evil (66+); cavern species are exempt (v7: alignment only limits taming).
cavern savagerycaverns ignore surface savagery: DF stocks savage cave species (giant cave spider) on calm forts.
extinct ruleDF's raws tag every real-world-extinct species SAVAGE; the world's REAL_WORLD_EXTINCT setting is read in place of that tag (UNTAMED_WILDS and ISOLATED: savage regions only; WILDERNESS and DOMESTICATED: any wild region). Extinct animal people stay savage-only, as all animal people.
extinct settingregion19's REAL_WORLD_EXTINCT cannot be read without DF (world.raws.param_real_world_extinct); the real forts assume UNTAMED_WILDS, the install's default preset value.
wilda creature is wild when it has a BIOME and either LARGE_ROAMING or a vermin tag, colony insects (VERMIN_SOIL_COLONY: ants, bees, termites) included (DF's own test for region populations).

Building it into seasonal-wildlife

A pass through the engine (scripts/seasonal-wildlife.lua on v7.4-onebuilder 834f92e, 19,102 lines; line numbers below) for the shortest path from today's code to the patterns on this page. Most of the machinery exists: the engine already scans every raw creature against the embark's biomes, already creates population entries on land and in caverns, and already places units with an on-site population reference. Order matters: each phase can ship and be checked on the rig before the next.

Decided (12 Oct)

  • The casts are not redrawn each year (9 Oct ruling stands). What resets at each new year is the draw: every cast species' arrival odds and its population entry go back to their start-of-year values (the ladder's FREQUENCY, the entry quantity and the reserve), so a species used up during the year arrives as often next year as this year. Where: a year hook beside the season timer (V7.ST), calling castLadder 8712 and CAVERN.apply 3795 on the kept casts and restocking from the reserve (applyLive 3100, RESERVE 3039). Phase 3.
  • Created entries are removed when the tool is turned off. The tool records every entry it creates (region tile, race, master and live row) in its saved config; off zeroes them, lets or sends their units off the map, clears any unit's population reference to them, and then deletes both rows, next to the reserve give-back (RESERVE.giveBack 3071). A unit still pointing at a deleted entry is the risk to test first. Phase 5.

Still open

  • Freshwater feature entries. Lake, river and pool species live on water-feature entries, which the engine cannot create yet. The ocean is easier: DF keeps sea life on land entries, which addNewSpecies already makes.
  • The audit's proposals (above): which promotions and wires to adopt. For a wired species, whether DF sends a wave from a created entry when its raws do not name the biome decides between an entry and placement (a rig test).

Method notes

Raws. DF 53.16's vanilla and extinct creature files compiled as DF compiles them (COPY_TAGS_FROM, the GIANT and ANIMAL_PERSON variations, castes, derived flags, aggregate biome tokens expanded), as in the earlier trace. Classification (guild, habitat, size, pet value, the 83 extinct corrections) is the engine's classify, mirrored in scripts/castsim/engine.py. The design is scripts/castsim/design.py; the runner is design_run.py. Random draws are seeded per embark, layer and season, so one run is one possible year.
